newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha Motor sees higher 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha Motor sees higher 1997 sales.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it forecast its calendar 1997 domestic motorcycle sales at 360,000 units, up 2.86 percent from a year earlier.
Its domestic sales fell 3.58 percent in 1996 to 350,000 units.
The world's second biggest motorcycle maker also forecast its 1997 overseas sales at 380,000 motorcycles, up 5.56 percent from 1996, due to strong demand in Europe. Exports rose 9.09 percent in 1996.

Yamaha's exports of motorcycle kit parts for overseas assembly were projected to rise 8.69 percent in 1997 to 2.50 million sets, reflecting higher production in Asia, after a 6.12 percent decline in 1996.
Yamaha estimated its domestic sales of electric power-assisted bicycles (PAS) at 115,000 units in 1997, up 144.68 percent, following a 7.84 percent decline the year before.
In November, Yamaha said it would launch a new, cheaper electric power-assisted bicycle on January 15 with an annual sales target of 100,000 units.
